The boat I am describing is a modern carbon-fiber powerboat, with a single diesel engine and no sails at all. It has one mast fitted with a radar dish and a glass cabin window towards the bow. The hull is made of fiberglass painted matte black, with a sharp, red stern. The ship's interior is spacious and brand new, with a large berth, an electric stove, and a full galley kitchen, complete with a digital navigation screen facing the helm.

The deck is narrow and cramped, with room for only two people and no benches. A large enclosed wheelhouse blocks most of the view and provides shelter from the rain. Up on the bow there is a short, retractable anchor arm, which can reach only a few feet over the water.

The boat has little character, its paint still shiny and untouched after only a few months of use. It runs on fuel rather than wind, a reminder that sailing has disappeared from modern boats entirely. From the loud morning engine to the still afternoon, this vessel is a disposable machine with few stories to tell.
